faq.q: Do I need a full re-roof or just repairs?
faq.a: It depends on the age and condition of your roof. We'll inspect it and tell you straight, no upselling. If it's past its best, a full re-roof is cheaper in the long run than endless repairs.

faq.q: Why should I pay more when I can get a cheaper quote?
faq.a: Cheap quotes often mean cheap materials or cowboys who vanish after taking your deposit. We give you a fixed price upfront, so you know what you're paying for. No surprises, no extra costs.

faq.q: Do you ask for a deposit?
faq.a: No. We don't ask for money upfront. You pay when the job is done, so you know the work is finished before you hand over a penny.

faq.q: How long does a re-roof take?
faq.a: Most re-roofs take 3 to 5 days, depending on the size of your home. We'll give you a clear timeline before we start, so you know what to expect.

faq.q: What happens if it rains while you're working?
faq.a: We cover the roof with tarpaulins to keep your home dry. If the weather's really bad, we'll pause the job and come back when it's safe to work.
Yes. We give you a written guarantee for the work, so you're covered if anything goes wrong. No vague promises, just proper paperwork.

blog_posts.title: When to replace your roof instead of repairing it
blog_posts.excerpt: Signs that a full re-roof is better than patch repairs.
blog_posts.body:
Small leaks or missing tiles might seem like minor issues, but they can hide bigger problems. If your roof is over 20 years old or has widespread damage, patch repairs may only delay the inevitable.

A full re-roof ensures all weak points are addressed at once. This prevents water damage to your home's structure and avoids the cost of repeated call-outs for temporary fixes.

We inspect every roof ourselves before quoting. If a repair will last, we'll tell you. If a replacement is the smarter choice, we'll explain why and give you a fixed price upfront.

blog_posts.title: How to spot a roofing cowboy before they take your deposit
blog_posts.excerpt: Red flags to watch for when hiring a roofer.
blog_posts.body:
Cowboy roofers often pressure you into quick decisions. They might offer a 'today-only' discount or demand a large deposit before starting work. Genuine roofers will give you time to think and won't ask for money upfront.

Check for a local address and landline number. If they only have a mobile, it's harder to track them down if things go wrong. Ask for photos of their previous work and references from recent customers.

We provide a written quote with a fixed price, no deposit, and our name on every roof we work on. If something feels off, walk away.
